title: Coefficient transport of the compact-support Thom computation for relative affine space
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $q=p^a$ with $a\geq1$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{k_0}$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$, as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and $m\geq0$. Write $\pi_m:\mathbf A^m_Y\to Y$ for the projection [def-sbc-affine-space]. Use the derived-complete, rationalized and common-stage categories of [def-pur-conventions], their compact-support functors [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and their coefficient units and Tate twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. For $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ the normalized affine-space integration map of [det-sp-trace-basic] is an isomorphism
$$t_{m,\Lambda}:R\pi_{m!}\Lambda_{\mathbf A^m_Y}(m)[2m]\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_Y,$$
equivalently $R\pi_{m!}\Lambda_{\mathbf A^m_Y}\cong\Lambda_Y(-m)[-2m]$. The integral map has, under the canonical derived reduction comparisons, the finite normalized integration maps $t_{m,A_{E,n}}$ as all its reductions. The rational and algebraically closed maps are its scalar transports. These comparisons are compatible with change of finite coefficient field. At $m=0$ the map is the identity.

source.place: Proof, first and second paragraphs: explicitly required algebraically closed coefficient transport of the compact-support Thom isomorphism; normalized coefficient transport also in sec-smooth-purity/sk-def-sp-trace/sk-def-sp-trace-properties.proof.md, clause (2).

proof.text: For every $m\geq0$, the projection $\pi_m:\mathbf A^m_Y\to Y$ is separated and of finite type, and it is smooth of pure relative dimension $m$ by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. Thus it is in the domain of the finite-coefficient purity and trace statements. At a finite coefficient level $A=A_{E,n}$, apply [thm-pur-vector-bundle-thom] to the trivial rank-$m$ vector bundle $\mathbf A^m_Y\to Y$ with its zero section. Its Thom morphism $A_Y\to R\pi_{m!}A_{\mathbf A^m_Y}(m)[2m]$ is an isomorphism, with inverse the vector-bundle trace. Clause (2) of [det-sp-trace-basic] identifies this trace with the normalized affine-space integration map $t_{m,A}$ and says that its geometric-fibre origin class maps to $1$; for $m=0$ the same clause and the identification $\mathbf A^0_Y=Y$ give the identity map. Hence the finite normalized map is an isomorphism in every degree $m$.

source.place: First paragraph: compact-support Thom computation on the affine fibre, specialized to the trivial rank-m bundle

proof.text: At integral coefficients, the map $t_{m,\mathcal O_E}$ is the smooth trace of the same projection, expressed through the derived-complete compact-support construction of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. The integral purity comparison of [thm-pur-adic-reconstruction] has finite reductions equal to the normalized finite-level purity comparisons, and [prop-pur-adic-reconstruction-trace-coherence] states that the corresponding smooth traces commute with this reconstruction. The finite-reduction theorem [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity] gives the same compatibility for the trace and affine orientation: under the canonical reduction comparison, the reduction of $t_{m,\mathcal O_E}$ is exactly $t_{m,A_{E,n}}$ for every $n$. These form a morphism of the strict reduction towers defining the integral compact-support objects. Every component is an isomorphism by Step 1, so the induced map on derived limits is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso]. Its normalization is inherited from the finite origin-class normalization in Step 1.

source.place: Clause (2), coefficient transport of the normalized affine-space trace through the coherent finite-level tower

proof.text: For $\Lambda=E$, the rational category and its compact-support functor are obtained by scalar localization of the integral constructions. [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity] transports the integral purity isomorphism to the rational and algebraically closed coefficient stages, while [prop-pur-rational-purity-trace-coherence] says that these transported purity maps commute with the smooth trace. The scalar-localization result [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] therefore identifies $t_{m,E}$ with the scalar transport of $t_{m,\mathcal O_E}$, so it is an isomorphism. The same argument at a common finite stage, followed by the common-stage construction of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ clause of [thm-pur-rational-and-qbar-purity], identifies $t_{m,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ with the scalar transport of the integral map and proves it is an isomorphism.

source.place: Clauses (2)-(3), rationalization and common-stage coefficient transport

proof.text: The transports are coherent when the finite coefficient field changes. For finite extensions $E\subset F$, [lem-pur-adic-scalar-trace-coherence] gives the explicit equality identifying the $F$-integral trace with the scalar extension of the $E$-integral trace, after the canonical twist and compact-support comparisons. Its finite-level reductions are the corresponding coefficient comparisons from [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison], and in the prime-power finite model the same normalization is the finite-free trace-extension identity of [lem-pur-finite-universal-smooth-trace]. The associativity and unit laws for rational scalar extension in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] transport these equalities to successive finite coefficient fields and to the common algebraic closure. Thus all coefficient versions of $t_m$ satisfy the stated change-of-field compatibility.

source.place: Clause (2), coefficient transport and compatibility with change of finite coefficient field

proof.text: Finally, tensoring the isomorphism $t_{m,\Lambda}:R\pi_{m!}\Lambda(m)[2m]\to\Lambda_Y$ with the inverse Tate twist and inverse cohomological shift gives $R\pi_{m!}\Lambda\simeq\Lambda_Y(-m)[-2m]$; this is the equivalent formulation in the statement. For $m=0$ all twists and shifts are units and the comparison is the identity already established in Step 1.

source.place: Second paragraph: rewriting the Thom isomorphism as the untwisted compact-support formula

proof_origin.place: First and second paragraphs, with coefficient transport expanded using the normalized trace transport statements of the purity chapter
